title: DR1 keeps a running "N selected" list of the species chosen so far, each removable and with a Clear all button; the frontend has nothing of the kind on its commodity page.

finding.frontend: Nothing on the commodity page reports what the user has chosen. The ticked checkboxes are the only record, and because the whole catalogue is on screen at once they are scattered through five fieldsets; a user with selections in three groups has to scroll the page to see them. There is no remove control and no clear-all control. The commodity template ends at the checkbox loop, the help details and the save buttons (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:20-36).
finding.prototype: Below the search box DR1 keeps a selection panel that appears as soon as anything is ticked. It is headed with the count — "3 selected" — lists the chosen species grouped under the commodity name and code, gives each one its own remove control labelled for that species, and carries a Clear all button in the panel header (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:100-108). It is needed because the result list is transient: a second search replaces the first list, so without the panel the earlier selections would leave the screen.
finding.difference: Add a selection summary beneath the commodity search: a count heading, the chosen species grouped by commodity name and code, a per-species remove control with a name a screen reader can distinguish, and a Clear all button, all hidden while nothing is selected. This only earns its place once the option list is a search result rather than the whole catalogue, so schedule it with commodities--commodity-search; on today's static list it would duplicate what the ticks already show.
finding.falsifiedBy: Ticking a species on DR1's commodity page and finding no panel appears beneath the search box. Neither captured DR1 state has anything selected, so both show the panel hidden; the behaviour was read from the prototype's own commodity-search script, which sets the panel's hidden attribute from whether any selection exists.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both full-page screenshots, then ran the falsifier the only way the evidence allows — against the prototype's own script, app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:443-481. It sets the panel's hidden attribute from whether anything is selected, writes "<count> selected" into the heading, groups the chosen species under "<name> (<code>)", renders a per-species remove button carrying a visually-hidden "Remove <label>", and unhides the Clear all button only when a selection exists. Every element the prose describes is present but hidden in both captured DR1 states at dr1-what-are-you-importing.html:100-108, so the markup is observable even though the populated state is not. On the frontend side the template genuinely ends where the finding says: fe-commodity-search.html goes from the last fieldset to the details block to the save buttons, with no panel, no remove control and no clear-all. Confidence "medium" is honest and better than a "high" here — the populated DR1 panel is unphotographed and the falsifier names exactly that. CORRECT.
finding.correction: Nothing wrong with the claim. One mechanical caveat: the named control "Clear all" carries a hidden attribute in both captured DR1 states, so it has no box for the crop step to find and this finding will fall back to the whole-page shots. That is the right picture for an add-section finding about a whole panel — and naming no control would give the same result — but the control name will not do the work the naming rule intends, and nobody should read the whole-page shot as a crop failure.

relatedTo.why: the panel exists because a search result list is transient; it has no job while the whole catalogue is on screen
